Good day. This is Sultana Al-Qahtani with the Sahel Desk.

Daily bottom line for 2026-10-27: Reporting dated 2026-10-27 gives the desk 3 incident accounts to examine in Burkina Faso and Niger. 2 have support from separate sources. The record is provisional; it does not establish the full extent of violence that day.

Mali: 9 retained reports. 1. Mali: A convoy of 1107 tankers filled with fuel arrives in Bamako. Mali: A convoy of 1107 fuel-filled tankers arrives in Bamako In Mali, the state continues to ensure fuel supply in the capital Bamako and the rest of the country. On the morning of yesterday, Monday, October 26, 2026, an impressive convoy of 1,107 tanker trucks filled with fuel arrived in the city of the three caimans ,under military escort . This is the largest convoy that Bamako has hosted since the beginning of this month of October, according to the Directorate General of Trade, Consumer Affairs and Competition. 2. Macina: humanitarian emergency intensifies for 542 displaced people from Souleye. Fleeing the attack on their village on September 3, 542 residents of Souleye, in the Ségou region, found refuge in Macina. Saturated houses, lack of food and difficulties in accessing school and social services: there are many needs. Despite the solidarity of local populations and the support of humanitarians, reception conditions remain difficult Forced to flee in a hurry, Souleye residents abandoned their homes, property and livelihoods. 3. Tafouk TV, the new media arm of Moscow-backed Sahelian juntas. Launched by the military regimes of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, Tafouk TV aims to impose the Alliance of Sahel States’ sovereignty-focused narrative. Encouraged by Russia, the broadcaster is emerging as repression against local journalists intensifies.

Burkina Faso: 5 retained reports. 1. Burkina Faso: 12 Beninese arrested in an alleged fraud case. Douze ressortissants béninois sont interpellés à Gaoua, dans le sud-ouest du Burkina Faso. Ils sont soupçonnés d’avoir monté deux réseaux d’arnaque qui profitaient de la crédulité de personnes en quête de protection selon l’Agence d’Information du Burkina Faso. Les interpellations ont eu lieu les 21 et 22 octobre 2026, a annoncé mardi le chef du Service régional de la police judiciaire (SRPJ) du Djôrô, le capitaine Théophile Zongo. 2. Burkina Faso: 12 suspected crooks arrested in Gaoua. Twelve suspected fraudsters of Beninese nationality were arrested on 21 and 22 October 2026 in Gaoua in south-west Burkina Faso by the Regional Judicial Police Service (SRPJ) of Djôrô, reports the AIB, on Tuesday 27 October. 3. Justice. In Burkina Faso, a new Penal Code reinstates the death penalty International mail. Abolished in 2018, then mentioned again in December 2025, the death penalty was reinstated in the new version of the Burkinabe Criminal Code adopted by the deputies on October 20. It must now be promulgated by the President, Ibrahim Traoré. The death penalty “is provided in particular for acts of terrorism, treason, espionage, assassination, parricide and certain other serious crimes,” details Studio Yafa The text provides for the execution of this sentence, "shooting, lethal injection, hanging or electrocution", adds the media of the Swallow Foundation.

Niger: 32 retained reports. 1. Niger denounces a drone attack by Chad with "the support of France". The facts date back to October 24 at 1am in the Emi Lulu area, in the Agadez region, not far from the Algerian border. This drone strike was carried out "from Chad" with "the support of France", according to the Nigerien government and left two civilians dead and wounded . Niamey speaks of an act of aggression, a violation of his national sovereignty and announces referral to the United Nations Security Council, the Peace and Security Council of the African Union invoking the UN Charter and the founding principles of the AU. 2. Chadian drone strikes in Niger: CODDAE calls for increased vigilance at national level. Niamey, Oct 27 (ANP)- The Collective for the Defense of the Right to Energy CODDAE issued a press release on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, denouncing the aggression of the drone from Chad during the night of October 24 to 25 that hit the Emi Lulu area. This attack, the statement reports, “clearly seeks to open a new front against Niger and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), which strengthens our sacred union” To this end, the Collective calls on the Nigerien population to strengthen national vigilance in the face of this attempt to sow terror. 3. Image Africa Niger: Chad denies any involvement in "drone strikes" on its soil with the "support" of France. On Tuesday, October 27, Chad rejected accusations from Niger, a neighboring country with which relations have been tense for several months. The latter accuses him of having killed two civilians in a "drone strike" on Nigerien soil with the "support" of France. Through its spokesperson, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, N’Djamena categorically denied Niamey's accusations about a drone strike on Nigerian soil on Monday, October 26 .

Mali.summary: Mali: FAMa strikes several terrorist positions in Koulikoro and Mopti The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, carried out several strikes against suspected terrorist groups in the Koulikoro and Mopti regions on 24 and 25 October 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the intelligence collected on 24 October made it possible to locate a group of terrorist elements with motorcycles and logistical means, about two kilometres south-west of the village of Kenenkoun, in the Koulikoro region.

Mali.title: A record for Bamako: 1,107 tankers secured by our valiant FAMa!
Mali.summary: This Monday, October 26, 2026, at around 8 a.m., a convoy of 1,107 tankers arrived in the parking lots of Bamako, after crossing the night under the escort of our valiant Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), which we salute for their commitment and courage . It is an exceptional volume: the largest convoy received in the capital since the beginning of October, after those of: October 3: 643 tanks; October 10: 957 tanks: October 17: 734 tanks.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa neutralize several terrorist positions in Koulikoro and Mopti
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On October 24, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, about 2 km southwest of the village of Kenenkoun, in the Koulikoro region, a point of regroupment of terrorist elements with several motorcycles as well as logistical means.

Mali.title: Security situation: the army draws up a new inventory
Mali.summary: AT THIS TIME, the Directorate of Information and Public Relations of the Armed Forces (DIRPA) held its traditional press briefing on the security situation, the operations carried out and those in progress throughout the territory. The consolidation of military positions in Kidal is one of the highlights of the period According to the Director of DIRPA, Colonel-Major Bakary Bocar Maïga, the offensive launched on October 6 as part of the "Dougoukoloko" operation allowed the FAMa to strengthen their system in the city and its surroundings.

Mali.title: Mali: a convoy of 1,107 tankers arrives in Bamako
Mali.summary: Mali: a convoy of 1,107 tanker trucks arrives in Bamako A convoy of 1,107 tanker trucks arrived in Bamako this Monday, October 26, 2026, at around 8 a.m., after a night journey under the escort of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). Mali.summary: Hundreds of displaced families from Yemen's Taiz and Lahj governorates are living in camps in Aden amid difficult living conditions and a continuing need for humanitarian assistance following a major Houthi offensive that started in September. In the Ras Imran area of Al-Buraiqeh district, the Al-Firdaws 1 and Al-Firdaws 2 camps contain approximately 850 tents sheltering displaced families.

Burkina Faso.title: 66th anniversary of the national armed forces: The garrison of Dédougou begins its preparations with a popular cross-country
Burkina Faso.summary: The National Armed Forces launched, in Dédougou, in the Bankui region, the regional activities commemorating the 66th anniversary of their creation, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, through a popular cross-country race followed by an aerobics session . As a prelude to the regional celebration of the 66th anniversary of the existence of the Burkinabe National Army on November 1, several preparatory activities are on display in Bankui and Sourou.

Niger.title: Algeria To Deploy Troops To Niger In First Foreign Mission In 53 Years
Niger.summary: By Enyichukwu Enemanna Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973. The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger’s defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria.

Niger.title: Algeria-Niger: a first Algerian military deployment abroad
Niger.summary: Pour la première fois de son histoire, l'Algérie s'apprête à déployer des troupes hors de ses frontières. Le Parlement algérien a approuvé l'envoi de militaires au Niger, pays voisin confronté à une insécurité persistante due aux attaques de groupes djihadistes et à l'instabilité dans plusieurs régions du nord. Cette décision marque un tournant majeur dans la doctrine de défense algérienne et ouvre un nouveau chapitre dans les relations entre Alger et Niamey.

Niger.summary: Algeria’s President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has ordered troops to neighbouring Niger to protect energy and economic interests shared by both countries. The decision, announced by Algeria’s presidency on Monday, came after both chambers of parliament approved the deployment in an emergency session on Sunday. Niger.summary: The Directorate General of Resources of the Ministry of the Interior received, this Monday, October 26, 2026, a batch of equipment composed of 120 4×4 Sinotruk pickups intended for the National Guard of Niger and the National Police, as well as 100 motorcycles for the Road Police unit . Acquired from the State's own funds, this equipment aims to strengthen the operational capacities of the security forces in their missions of protecting people and property and defending territorial integrity .

Niger.summary: - Military cooperation between Algeria and Niger: The decision came after the signing of a joint military agreement, and the Algerian parliament voted in favor of it, reflecting a new stage of security and defense cooperation to secure joint projects in light of security threats.

Niger.summary: Niamey, Oct 26 (ANP)- The Director General of Resources of the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration, Commander Hamidou Soumana, received, this Monday, October 26, 2026, a batch of equipment composed of 120 4×4 vehicles and 100 motorcycles intended for the National Guard and the Road Police . The 120 4×4 vehicles are intended for the National Guard (GNN) and the 100 motorcycles for the Road Police unit.

Niger.title: Agadez/Security: In Bilma, Brigadier General Ibroh Amadou Bacharou reaffirms the CNSP's commitment to ensuring security in Niger
Niger.summary: Brigadier General Ibro Amadou Bacharou, Special Chief of Staff of the President of the Republic, accompanied by Brigadier General Abdourahamane Abou Zataka, Chief of Staff of the Army, and several civilian and military personalities, carried out, on Friday, October 23, 2026, a working mission to Dirkou, in the department of Bilma, Agadez region . This visit was marked by a collective prayer and a large popular meeting during which the administrative authorities and representatives of the populations expressed their concerns and reaffirmed their commitment to peace, security and the rebuilding of Niger .

Niger.title: Tillabéri/Infrastructure: Minister Salissou Mahaman Salissou assesses the work of the Farié-Téra road and the impact of the Garbougna structure
Niger.summary: The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, made a visit on Friday, October 23, 2026, to the Farié-Téra axis, in the Tillabéri region. On the agenda, the monitoring of the rehabilitation work of this road and the evaluation of a crossing structure built in Garbougna to end the seasonal isolation of this locality . Through these two stages, the Minister took stock of the achievements, the remaining work and the measures taken to continue the work in a difficult security context.

Niger.summary: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973 Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973. The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger's defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State.

Niger.title: Algerian parliament approves army deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: A military parade takes place during the 2026 graduation ceremony at the Houari-Boumediene Military Academy in Cherchell, Algeria on July 9, 2026. /VCG File Algerian lawmakers on Sunday approved deploying People's National Army detachments to Niger, according to official statements from both chambers of parliament. During closed-door sessions, Algeria's Council of the Nation and People's National Assembly, the upper and lower houses of parliament, respectively, validated the presidential notification submitted by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune under Article 91 of the Constitution.

Niger.title: Algerian upper house of parliament approves troop deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: Algeria’s upper house of parliament has approved deploying troops to Niger to protect its energy facilities. The country’s Council of Nations approved the deployment during an emergency session on Sunday, while the lower house is expected to hold a session on Monday. If the deployment is approved in the lower parliament, it means the country is highly likely to deploy troops to protect its facilities located along the border area in the north of Niger, particularly the Kafra oil region and other energy facilities linked to Algeria’s state-owned energy company Sonatrach.

Niger.title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment in over 50 years
Niger.summary: Algeria’s parliament on Sunday approved a resolution to send troops to Niger, making the first time Algerian soldiers will be deployed abroad since the 1973 Arab-Israeli war. Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including near its border with Algeria, and the deployment comes as Algiers and Niamey are building the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline after decades of delays.

Niger.title: Algeria’s military deployment to Niger: What’s behind the move?
Niger.summary: Algeria’s parliament has approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger, in a major shift in the North African nation’s noninterventionist military doctrine. Algeria’s lower house, the People’s National Assembly, ratified the deployment on Sunday after the upper house, the Council of the Nation, unanimously approved the proposal earlier in the day.

Niger.title: Africa: Algerian soldiers in Niger
Niger.summary: The Algerian Parliament unanimously approved on Sunday the deployment of units of the National People's Army in Niger. This would be Algeria's first military intervention abroad since sending troops in support of Egypt during the 1973 war . Algerian soldiers are to settle in Madama, in northern Niger, near the Libyan border, on the site of a former French base used during Operation Barkhane.

Niger.title: Algeria: Parliament approves deployment of troops to Niger
Niger.summary: On Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Algerian Parliament approved the sending of army units to Niger. This decision, which marks a break with the traditional doctrine of military non-intervention abroad, aims in particular to protect Algerian energy interests in the Sahelian country, Al Jazeera reports. Algeria reaches a major milestone in its military cooperation with Niger .

Niger.title: Sahel: Algerian parliament authorizes sending troops to Niger
Niger.summary: Algeria is taking a new step in its security rapprochement with Niger. On Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Council of the Nation, the upper chamber of the Algerian Parliament, unanimously approved a decision authorizing the dispatch of a detachment of the National People's Army (ANP) to Niger This initiative comes in a context of strengthening military cooperation between Algiers and Niamey, against the backdrop of security threats in the Sahel and strategic economic interests.

Niger.title: Military Adventure in Niger Threatens Algeria with Drowning in 'Swamp Coast'
Niger.summary: Algeria is venturing into one of the most volatile security environments in Africa, after the parliamentary approval announced on Sunday opened the door to sending army units to Niger, in a move that is difficult to separate from the decline of its diplomatic influence in the Sahel region, and its attempt to restore a regional position that has become vulnerable to changing alliances and escalating competition among external powers.

Niger.title: Algerian parliament votes to send soldiers to neighboring Niger
Niger.summary: The Council of the Nation, the upper house, and then the National People's Assembly, the lower house, both voted on Sunday to send military troops to Niger.

Niger.title: Border security and energy interests.. What is behind Algeria's decision to send troops to Niger?
Niger.summary: The Algerian parliament, in its two chambers, the People's National Assembly and the National Assembly, on Sunday, approved the request of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune to send units of the Algerian army to Niger, with the aim of protecting the strategic interests of the country and securing the investment projects of the state company Sonatrach, in response to a request from the Nigerian authorities.

Niger.title: Nigerien, 3 others nabbed over guard’s killing, theft
Niger.summary: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested a Niger Republic national and three others over the alleged killing of a security guard and theft of goods worth over N400 million in the state. The suspects, identified as Hamisu Nuhu, Suleiman Rabiu, Hussaini Gago, a Nigerien, and Ibrahim Haruna, were arrested in connection with a robbery at Paparazzi Communication Complex in Auchi, Etsako West Local Government Area, on July 12, 2026.

Mali.title: Mali: the death toll from last weekend's deadly attack rises to 54 (army)
Mali.summary: The Malian armed forces announced on Saturday that they had discovered 54 bodies after attacks on camps in the north-east of the country last weekend, bringing the death toll to six more. The attacks targeted the Menaka region of the troubled West African country, where gunmen reportedly arrived on motorcycles before opening fire on camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community It was within the Daoussahak community that the Armed Movement for the Salvation of Azawad (MSA), a group allied to the ruling junta in Mali, was born, according to security and community sources.

Mali.title: Mali: the Directorate of Human Resources of the Armed Forces towards a new status
Mali.summary: The Council of Ministers adopted a draft law amending the ordinance of 27 September 2017 establishing the Directorate of Human Resources of the Armed Forces (DRHA). The decision aims to adapt this structure to the reforms undertaken to modernize the Malian Armed Forces . Created to develop and monitor the implementation of the human resources management and development policy, the HRD faces shortcomings related to the evolution of the institutional and legal framework as well as the new requirements of the army.

Mali.title: Mali military reports 54 dead after attacks in northeast
Mali.summary: Mali's armed forces say the death toll from attacks on camps in the country's northeastern Menaka region has risen to 54, after six more bodies were discovered. The attacks occurred last weekend when armed men on motorcycles reportedly opened fire on camps mainly occupied by members of the Daoussahak community. Mali.title: KIDAL: the FAMa provide care and comfort to the populations of the camps
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), through the Directorate of the Armed Forces Health Service (DSSA) and their Russian partner, conducted, on Friday, October 23, 2026, a medical assistance operation for the benefit of the populations living in the localities located on the outskirts of the city of Kidal .

Mali.title: Mali: HRW accuses army of beating civilians, JNIM refuses to punish execution of prisoners

The NGO documents indiscriminate drone strikes by the Malian army and the execution of soldiers captured by JNIM and the Fla. HRW turns to the African Union, for lack of other interlocutor .

Niger.title: Algeria: Senate approves sending troops to Niger

Niger.title: Algeria: Parliament unanimously votes on a decision to send army units to Niger The decision to send Algerian troops to Niger came four days after the signing of a memorandum of understanding to strengthen military cooperation between Algiers and Niamey.

Mali.title: Bandiagara: one dead and one injured in an attack in Danlekanda
Mali.summary: One dead and one wounded by gunfire, this is the result of an attack perpetrated Thursday, October 22 by unidentified armed individuals against the village of Danlekanda, in the commune of Muétoumou, Bandiagara circle. The injured person was on his way to the Bandiagara referral health center. Last week, the village of Dôolo, in the same commune, recorded three deaths in another attack .

Mali.title: Speculations on Mali-Algeria border cooperation
Mali.summary: Recent strikes by Algeria against illegal gold miners in the south of the country feed the comments of Malian netizens who want to see the beginning of military cooperation in the border area, a traditional retreat base for fighters of the Azawad Liberation Front (Fla) . Conversely, Tuareg Fla sympathizers condemn this possible future rapprochement and resurrect old distrust of Algeria.

Mali.title: Mali-Qatar: security cooperation at the centre of exchanges
Mali.summary: The Minister of Security and Civil Protection, Major General Daoud Aly Mohammedine, received in audience, on 22 October 2026, Qatar's new ambassador to Mali, Ahmed Turki A. A. Alsobai.

Mali.title: Mali – Türkiye: Ambassador Efe CEYLAN received by Minister Daoud Aly MOHAMMEDINE to consolidate defence cooperation
Mali.summary: COOPERATION MALI TÜRKİYÉ: TOWARDS A STRENGTHENING OF the PARTNERSHIP IN the FIELD OF SECURITY The strengthening of security cooperation between Mali and Türkiye was at the heart of the audience granted, this Thursday, October 22, 2026, by the Minister of Security and Civil Protection, Major General Daoud Aly MOHAMMEDINE, to His Excellency Mr. Efe CEYLAN, Ambassador of the Republic of Türkiyé in Mali .

Mali.title: Mali Army, Russian Fighters Accused of Civilian Killings
Mali.summary: Human Rights Watch has accused Mali's armed forces and Russia-controlled Africa Corps of committing serious abuses against civilians in the central Mopti region during renewed fighting. The organisation said an apparent military drone strike on September 16 killed eight civilians and injured at least six others in Guélédié village. Witnesses reported that the strike hit an area where residents had gathered to access satellite internet, although armed fighters linked to al-Qaeda were reportedly present in the village.

Mali.title: Mali – Qatar: General Daoud Aly Mohammedine and the Qatari diplomat discuss security cooperation
Mali.summary: MALI QATAR: TOWARDS STRENGTHENING SECURITY COOPERATION The Minister of Security and Civil Protection, Major General Daoud Aly MOHAMMEDINE, received in audience, this Thursday, October 22, 2026, His Excellency Ahmed Turki A. A. ALSOBAI, new Ambassador of the State of Qatar in Mali .

Mali.title: Mali: Army, Russia's 'Africa Corps' Commit New Abuses
Mali.summary: Nairobi — Unlawful Drone Strike, Torture of Civilians in Mopti Region Mali's armed forces and the allied Russia-controlled Africa Corps have committed new atrocities against civilians in central Mali during renewed fighting, Human Rights Watch said today. On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others.

Mali.title: Mali: More than forty civilians killed on Sunday by armed men
Mali.summary: Mali : plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks carried out by armed men in the Ménaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacements, several security, local and civil society sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arriving on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, originates.

Mali.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men, according to security and local sources

Burkina Faso.title: Quarterly increase in the colours of the SDS: Burkinabe Customs at the rendezvous of patriotic duty
Burkina Faso.summary: This Friday, October 23, 2026, the Directorate General of Customs hosted the quarterly ceremony of raising the national colours of the Defence and Security Forces (FDS) and the Volunteers for the Defence of the Fatherland (VDP). This solemn meeting, marked by patriotism and brotherhood of arms, was held in a context marked by the commemoration of the 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina/Solidarity: A member of the diaspora provides support to widows and orphans who are victims of the war
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina/Solidarity: A member of the diaspora provides support to widows and orphans victims of the war ASVOVIG staff and donors In a show of solidarity with families affected by the war, Abdoul Dramane Guinko, a member of the Burkinabe diaspora, donated food to the Agency for the Support of Widows, Orphans and Victims of War (ASVOVIG), this Friday, October 23, 2026 in Ouagadougou Composed of rice, spaghetti and oil, this donation aims to support the families of war victims.

Burkina Faso.title: ‎Tenkodogo: Water and forest agents capture a crocodile near a chicken coop and release it into the dam
Burkina Faso.summary: Tenkodogo: Water and forestry officers capture a crocodile near a chicken coop and release it into the dam A crocodile lurking near a chicken coop in a courtyard in the Gommisi neighborhood, opposite the Tenkodogo Gendarmerie Group, was captured without incident on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and then released into the city dam . According to the Burkina news agency that reports the information, it was a resident who gave the alert to the competent services after seeing the reptile in the concession.

Niger.title: illabéri: the Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure visits the rehabilitation site of the Farié-Téra axis
Niger.summary: Tillabéri, Oct 23 (ANP) – The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou carried out, this Friday, October 23, 2026, a field visit to the rehabilitation site of the Farié-Téra road as well as at the Garbougna structure. The purpose of this visit was to inquire about the progress of the work and to assess the results obtained .

Niger.title: Defense: In the field of military operations, the SDF continues to maintain pressure on armed terrorist groups
Niger.summary: Despite the relative lull observed recently in the fight against security threats, the defense and security forces (FDS) remain mobilized on the various fronts of military operations where they continue to maintain pressure against armed terrorist groups (AGT) and other organized criminal groups .

Niger.title: Algeria and Niger sign 'Memorandum of Understanding' to strengthen military cooperation
Niger.summary: Since the reconciliation at the beginning of the year between the President of Niger, Abdourahamane Tiani, and that of Algeria, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, Niamey and Algiers have not left each other: in the space of a month, this is the second time that leaders of the armies of the two countries have met. A new exchange that ended this week with the signing of a memorandum of understanding on Algerian-Nigerian military cooperation In addition to the interview with his Algerian counterpart for Defence, Said Chengriha, the Nigerien Minister Salifou Modi was also received by President Tebboune.

Niger.title: Tillabéri: the Minister of Equipment notes the progress of the work on the Farié-Téra road
Niger.summary: The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, carried out this Friday, October 23, a field visit on the Fari-Tera road, in the Tillabéri region, to assess the progress of the rehabilitation work on this road and to note the state of a crossing work carried out in Garbou Gna for the benefit of the populations Accompanied by the Governor of the Tillabéri region, Colonel Maina Boukar, the Secretary General of the Governorate, officials of the Defence and Security Forces (FDS), the Prefect of the Department of Gothèye, as well as ministerial officials and departmental and…

Niger.title: Africa: Algeria and Niger sign "a memorandum of understanding" to strengthen their military cooperation
Niger.summary: The rapprochement between Algeria and Niger continues. After the visit of the President and the Prime Minister of Niger, the Minister of Defence was welcomed on 21 October in Algiers. With his Algerian counterpart, they signed a military agreement to strengthen security cooperation between the two countries This meeting comes barely two months after a mutiny in Niamey against the power of President Abdourahamane Tiani who has since received military support from Algiers.

Niger.summary: Algiers and Niamey deepen military cooperation as army chief Saïd Chengriha and defence minister Salifou Mody sign an agreement aimed at strengthening security ties amid regional threats.

Niger.title: Algeria-Niger: a military agreement that confirms the return of Algiers to the Sahel
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger signed a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation on the occasion of the visit to Algiers of the Nigerien Minister of Defence, General Salifou Mody. This rapprochement comes in a context of recomposition of security alliances in the Sahel, where Algiers seeks to consolidate its influence with the countries of the Alliance of Sahelian States (AES) Algeria and Niger have taken a new step in their security rapprochement with the signing, on Wednesday 21 October 2026 in Algiers, of a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation.

Institutional separation has not erased interdependencies Since the effective withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, the countries of both sets continue to share trade corridors, population movements and security challenges.

Mali.title: Arm of iron in Bamako: Seydou "Solution" against Mohamed "Lil Bougou", a contract signed on October 16
Mali.summary: The Malian sports arm wrestling federation recorded, on October 16, 2026, the signing of the contract for a fight between Seydou, known as "Solution", and Mohamed, known as "Lil Bougou". The two practitioners received a preparation bonus of 500,000 CFA francs each. The meeting, the date of which remains to be communicated, also provides for a bonus for the winner, the amount of which has not been made public .

Mali.title: Talhandak and Menaka. Targeted FAMa strikes neutralize several terrorists The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the public...
Mali.summary: In a press release published this Thursday, October 22, 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces informs that on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in the Talhandak sector, the tracking of two motorcyclists made it possible to identify, about 3 km northwest of Talhandak, a point of regroupment of terrorist individuals with several motorcycles and trying to hide under a vegetal cover .

Mali.title: Kayes: two suspects arrested for alleged supply of terrorist armed groups
Mali.summary: Kayes: two suspects arrested for an alleged supply of terrorist armed groups On 16 and 18 October 2026, the Police Station of the 2nd district of Kayes arrested two individuals suspected of supplying fuel to terrorist armed groups (GAT). The first suspect was arrested in Sintiani, on the Kayes-Melga axis, while carrying eight fuel cans concealed in a metal crate .

Mali.title: Mali.. Militants targeted in Tahandalek and Menaka during army operations
Mali.summary: On Thursday, the Malian Army announced the targeting of two military operations in the sectors of Tahandalek and Menaka, which resulted in the targeting of a gathering of militants and the destruction of a vehicle.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: two targeted strikes in Talhandak and Menaka
Mali.summary: According to the General Staff, the FAMa and their allies carried out two surgical strikes in Talhandak and Menaka on 20 and 21 October 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Tuesday, October 20, the tracking of two motorcyclists made it possible to spot a group of individuals presented as terrorists, with several motorcycles, about three kilometers northwest of Talhandak.

Mali.title: Mali: military operation targets' terrorists' near Ngoma Koura
Mali.summary: A strike by the Malian Armed Forces targeted a gathering of motorcyclists in the Ouagadou forest. In addition, the Malian army is continuing its reconnaissance to establish the toll of the strike. The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) announced that they had neutralized several fighters in a strike on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 near Ngoma Koura Indeed, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the target was a group gathered under a tree in the forest of Ouagadou.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike a terrorist position in the Ouagadou forest
Mali.summary: Thanks to the use of precise intelligence, the Malian Armed Forces continue their missions of surveillance and security of the national territory image illustration The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) continue their operations of surveillance, reconnaissance and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the exploitation of precise information allowed the units involved to locate a group of motorcyclists in the Ouagadou forest, near the village of Ngoma Koura.

Mali.title: Mali: Youssouf Toloba and Dan Na Ambassagou reaffirm their commitment to the homeland, peace and national unity
Mali.summary: Youssouf Toloba and Dan Na Ambassagou: a call for peace and the strengthening of security in Mali. Faced with disputed information about his alleged encirclement, Dan Na Ambassagou's Chief of Staff enjoys the support of his movement. In Bandiagara, hunters are calling for increased security, better coordination with FAMa and increased attention from Transitional Authorities .

Mali.title: Mali: FAMa strikes two terrorist targets in Talhandak and Menaka
Mali.summary: SECURING the NATIONAL TERRITORY: THE FAMa STRIKE TWO TERRORIST TARGETS IN TALHANDAK and the MENAKA SECTOR Operation Dougoukoloko: the Malian Armed Forces continue their missions of surveillance and neutralization of threats with method, precision and determination. BAMADA.NET – The dynamics of securing the national territory continues in Mali . As part of Operation Dougoukoloko, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), with the support of their partners, maintain their surveillance, control and reconnaissance missions in several areas of the country .

Mali.title: Mali: The FAMa hit a group of motorcyclists in the Ouagadou forest
Mali.summary: Mali: The FAMa hit a group of motorcyclists in the forest of Ouagadou The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) announce that they carried out a targeted strike on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, against a group of more than a dozen motorcyclists spotted in the forest of Ouagadou, near the village of Ngoma Koura According to our colleagues in Maliweb who cite the General Staff of the Armed Forces, several terrorist elements were neutralized during this operation carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko.

Mali.title: Jihadists blamed for Mali attack, 48 dead: sources
Mali.summary: Modern Ghana

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina: what the new Penal Code says
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso reinstates the death penalty in its new Penal Code, adopted unanimously. The Ministry of Justice detailed the main innovations. The Burkinabe Ministry of Justice published on its Facebook page on Wednesday a table of the innovations of the new Penal Code, adopted the day before by the 71 members of the People's Legislative Assembly.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: The country reinstates the death penalty (HRW)
Burkina Faso.summary: A scary message for critics of the junta in a context of widespread repression Burkina Faso's unelected parliament unanimously adopted a new penal code that reinstates the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and import of expired or prohibited products The country had abolished the death penalty for common crimes in 2018, while its last known judicial execution was in 1988.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina: The new Penal Code prohibits funerals for death row inmates, polyandry is now prohibited
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina : Le nouveau Code pénal proscrit les funérailles pour les condamnés à mort exécutés, la polyandrie désormais interdite Au Burkina Faso, l’Assemblée législative du Peuple (ALP) a adopté lors de sa plénière d’hier mardi 20 octobre, le projet de loi portant Code pénal. Ce nouveau texte comprend neuf livres, 33 titres et 97 chapitres, pour un total de plus de 900 articles.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Shooting, lethal injection, hanging... details of the procedure for executing the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The new Burkinabe Criminal Code provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty for several serious crimes and specifies the modalities of its execution. The innovations of the text, four modes of execution are planned: shooting, lethal injection, hanging and electrocution. The system also provides a framework for remedies and the case of pregnant convicted women Adopted unanimously by the 71 voters of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the new Penal Code marks an important development in Burkina Faso's criminal law.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty as Junta Tightens Grip
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso's unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code restoring the death penalty for offences including high treason, terrorism, espionage, parricide and importing expired or prohibited products. The death penalty for ordinary crimes was abolished in 2018. Human Rights Watch warns that reinstating capital punishment could further threaten civil liberties under the military junta, which took power in a 2022 coup.

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: a delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie in immersion at the gendarmerie of Burkina
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie is staying in Ouagadougou, as part of a working visit and consolidation of the partnership with the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso. This mission is led by Lieutenant General Aykut Tanriverdi, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of the Republic of Türkiye It is with the rise of colors, an act highly solemn and rich in symbols that the Turkish delegation began its immersion within the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: The main innovations of the new Penal Code
Burkina Faso.summary: The new Burkina Faso Penal Code adopted on 20 October 2026 by the People's Legislative Assembly introduces a dozen main innovations including the reinstatement of the death penalty for certain offences, the revision of financial sanctions related to the misappropriation of public funds, the creation of new offences and the raising of certain penalties. The amendments also concern road traffic, the environment, international crimes, protected animals and offences committed using information and communication technologies.

Niger.title: Two European Women Freed After Kidnap in Niger
Niger.summary: A Swiss woman and an Austrian woman kidnapped in Niger in 2025 have been released after spending more than a year in captivity, their respective governments have confirmed. The women, identified as 69-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Austrian citizen Eva Gretzmacher, arrived in Benghazi, eastern Libya, following their release, according to local media reports.

Niger.title: Niger and Algeria sign a memorandum of understanding in the field of military cooperation
Niger.summary: The Nigerien Minister of National Defence, Army General Salifou Modi is on a working visit to Algiers. It was yesterday Wednesday, October 21, at the headquarters of the General Staff of the People's National Army (ANP) . After saluting the national flag, listening to the two national anthems and presenting military honours, the Nigerien official had a meeting with Said Chanegriha, Minister Delegate to the Algerian Minister of National Defence, Chief of Staff of the National People's Army .

Niger.title: Haftar stages the release in Benghazi of two hostages kidnapped in Niger
Niger.summary: The two women abducted in 2025 in Agadez, the capital of northern Niger, were released on Wednesday by their captors from the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS), thanks to the good offices of Libyan Marshal and Eastern strongman Khalifa Haftar. Austria's Eva Gretzmacher and Switzerland's Claudia Abbt thank Haftar father and son in the video below, broadcast by al-Masar TV, a Benghazi TV, on platform X .

Niger.title: Algeria and Niger sign "a security pact"
Niger.summary: The Chief of Staff of the Algerian National People's Army and the Nigerien Minister of State in charge of National Defence met in Algiers. Algeria, strongly encouraged by Russia, continues its rapprochement with the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) On 21 October, Niger's Minister of State for National Defence, Salifou Mody, visited Algiers for the second time in two weeks.

Niger.title: Algeria-Niger: a memorandum of understanding to strengthen military cooperation
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger signed, Wednesday, October 21, 2026, a memorandum of understanding to strengthen their military cooperation The document was initialled by Army General Said Chanegriha, Algerian Minister Delegate to the Minister of National Defence and Chief of Staff of the People's National Army, and Army General Salifou Modi, Nigerien Minister of Defence, on a working visit to Algeria at the head of a large delegation According to Said Chanegriha, this visit reflects the desire of the two countries to consolidate their military cooperation and to meet together the security challenges with efficiency and…

Niger.title: Niger: 12 dead in an armed attack on two passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez axis (governor)
Niger.summary: Maliweb

Niger.title: Algeria and Niger sign a memorandum of military cooperation
Niger.summary: Maliweb

Niger.title: Niger: the two European hostages kidnapped by EIGS in Agadez now free after several months of captivity
Niger.summary: Announced as free for a few days, it was on Wednesday 21 October that the two (02) European hostages, Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt, kidnapped in 2025 in Agadez by the EIGs, reappeared after several months of captivity. They were handed over to the authorities in Benghazi, Libya, before their scheduled return to the country this Thursday, October 22, 2026 .

Niger.title: Military cooperation: Niamey and Algiers sign a new agreement that strengthens their partnership in the fields of Defence and Security
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger have just signed a new memorandum of understanding on military cooperation which strengthens relations between the two countries in the fields of defence and security.

Niger.title: Niger: Two Western hostages released in Libya after more than 18 months in Islamic State captivity
Niger.summary: Claudia Abbt and Eva Gretzmacher, held hostage by Islamic State in Niger, have been freed and flown to Benghazi following mediation led by Saddam Haftar, who is using the breakthrough to expand his political influence across the Sahel.

Niger.title: Swiss and Austrian women in Libya after release from Niger kidnap ordeal
Niger.summary: An Austrian and a Swiss women kidnapped in Niger more than a year and a half ago have been freed and are in Libya, Bern and Vienna announced Thursday. Sixty-nine-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Eva Gretzmacher arrived in the eastern city of Benghazi where they received medical treatment. Their release follows an intervention by Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, who controls the east and parts of the south of the country.

Niger.title: Two former European hostages kidnapped in Niger in 2025 have been released and are in Libya
Niger.summary: Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt, two European women kidnapped in the Sahel in 2025, are free, a Libyan television channel has announced. The announcement was confirmed Thursday, October 22 thanks to images of the two ex-hostages who arrived in Benghazi Because it was through the strong man of eastern Libya, Marshal Khalifa Haftar, that they regained their freedom.

Niger.title: Read more: Swiss and Austrian hostages freed in Niger
Niger.summary: Swiss and Austrian hostages freed in Niger Two European nationals, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman, who were kidnapped in Niger over a year ago, have been released. They have arrived in Benghazi, in eastern Libya, a local television channel announced during the night between Wednesday and Thursday. “Two hostages, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman, have been released after a year and a half in captivity in Niger and have arrived in Benghazi thanks to the intervention of the Deputy Commander-in-Chief,” Saddam Haftar, deputy commander-in-chief of Libya’s armed forces, said Libyan television Al-Masar announced.

Niger.title: Mali: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches - What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed (African Arguments)
Niger.summary: The mutiny that broke out in air base 101 in Niamey in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the 'jihadists.' For all of the Sahel, it's a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.

Niger.title: Two European Hostages Freed in Niger
Niger.summary: Two European women abducted in Niger in 2025 have been released after spending more than a year in captivity, according to Libyan media reports. Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian citizen Claudia Abbt, 69, arrived in the eastern Libyan city of Benghazi following their release. Libya’s eastern-based Al-Masar TV reported that the two women had been freed after being held hostage in Niger for about a year and a half.

Niger.title: Niger-Algeria military cooperation: a new strategic partnership for the security of the Sahel and regional sovereignty
Niger.summary: The signing of a military cooperation protocol between Niamey and Algiers marks a new stage in the rapprochement between the two countries. Faced with cross-border security challenges, this initiative opens up prospects for consultation and collaboration, in a region where States intend to have greater control over their strategic choices and strengthen their defence capacities BAMADA.NET - Regional cooperation in the field of defence remains a major issue for Sahel-Saharan countries.

Niger.title: Niger-Libya: Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt released and arrived in Benghazi
Niger.summary: Austria's Eva Gretzmacher and Switzerland's Claudia Abbt, kidnapped separately in Agadez in 2025, were released and arrived in Benghazi, eastern Libya, on Wednesday, 21 October. Their submission to the Austrian and Swiss authorities must take place after the completion of the necessary formalities . According to our information, a plane was to leave Benghazi on Thursday, October 22, stop in Vienna to hand over Eva Gretzmacher to the Austrian authorities, then continue to Switzerland with Claudia Abbt.

These operations are part of the sustained efforts made by the regional authorities, in synergy with the Defence and Security Forces (FDS), to dismantle the logistical support networks for the Armed Terrorist Groups (AGTS) and to hinder their supply chains .

Mali.title: Transition Support Fund: The moto-taximan Dramane Kamiya makes a contribution of 100,000 CFA francs
Mali.summary: Bamako, October 21, 2026 (AMAP)– Dramane Kamiya, a 49-year-old motorcycle taxi driver, contributed 100,000 FCFA to the Transition Support Fund. He presented his donation on Wednesday to the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, during a ceremony organized at the Primature, noted AMAP . A father living in Badalabougou, the donor explained that he wanted to contribute to national recovery efforts, despite the modesty of his daily income.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: several terrorist elements neutralized in the Ouagadou Forest
Mali.summary: Bamako, October 21, 2026 (AMAP) - The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, have successfully carried out an action against a group of motorcyclists in the Ouagadou forest, near the village of Ngoma Koura, the General Staff of the Armed Forces announced in a statement released Wednesday. According to the press release, this operation is part of the ongoing surveillance, control and security of the national territory carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Germany: Students call for protest on October 31, police fear excesses
Mali.summary: Bamako, October 21 (AMAP) The student collective "Gen Z steht auf" called for national demonstrations on October 31 in Germany to denounce cuts in spending on education and social services, the rising cost of living and plans to restore compulsory military service, reports the Anadolu Agency . Gatherings are planned in Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Munich and other cities across the country.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: several fighters neutralized in the Ouagadou forest
Mali.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: several neutralized fighters in the forest of Ouagadou On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) struck a group of motorcyclists spotted in the forest of Ouagadou, near the village of Ngoma Koura. According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, several terrorist elements were neutralized during this operation . This action is part of Operation Dougoukoloko, conducted to strengthen the surveillance and security of the national territory.

Mali.title: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State militants kill at least 48 civilians in Ménaka
Mali.summary: The Idaksahak pastoralist community was targeted in an apparent revenge attack following military operations, raising fears of further bloodshed in northeastern Mali.

Mali.title: Benbere platform fights disinformation in Mali
Mali.summary: It is increasingly difficult for young people, in the Sahel countries as elsewhere, to distinguish between information and disinformation. Young people are really at the heart of the dynamics of fake news because they are, first of all, the main target, on social networks that have become the main source of information for adolescents and young adults But young people are also key players in the fight against disinformation.

Mali.title: Ouagadou Forest: The FAMa neutralize a major terrorist column
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the use of precise information made it possible to detect and follow several columns of motorcyclists moving in the Ouagadou forest, near the village of Ngoma Koura.

Mali.title: Mali: About forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men in the Ménaka region
Mali.summary: In Mali, the Executive Office of the Idaksahak community expressed on Monday "its strong emotion and its immense dismay" after the death of 48 civilians of the community, last Sunday, on the side of Tagadayat, in the region of Menaka. According to their statement, "these defenceless civilian populations were attacked by armed elements of Daesh [Islamic State group, editor's note], arrived on board several motorcycles" .

Mali.title: Mali: 69 soldiers appear before the military justice, several crimes are accused
Mali.summary: Since Monday 19 October 2026 in Sévaré, the Military Court of Mopti has examined 43 cases involving 72 defendants, including 69 military personnel. The Malian military justice system is examining several cases with different stakes. Open on Monday, October 19 in Sévaré, in central Mali, the correctional and criminal session of the Military Court of Mopti is to continue until October 29 A total of 43 cases involving 72 people are on the list, according to information from the military prosecutor's office reported by the Malian Press Agency (AMAP).

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Kenya: Paul Mackenzie and 28 other defendants convicted for the murder of 192 children and one adult
Mali.summary: Bamako, Oct 21 (AMAP) A Kenyan court on Monday found Pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 other defendants guilty of the murder of 192 children and an adult in the Shakahola massacre, a tragedy that killed more than 400 people, according to Kenyan authorities “I am satisfied that the prosecution has proved the facts against the 29 defendants for the murder of 192 children and one adult in accordance with section 203 of the Criminal Code,” said High Court Judge Diana Kavedza-Mochache when the verdict was delivered.

Mali.title: Image Published on October 21, 2026 Africa Burkina Faso: the death penalty reinstated by the military government of Ibrahim Traoré eight years after its abolition Burkina Faso reinstated, on Tuesday, October 21, the death penalty, abolished in 2018, in a new Penal Code, voted unanimously by the 71 non-member...
Mali.summary: Burkina Faso reinstated, on Tuesday, October 21, the death penalty, abolished in 2018, in a new Penal Code, voted unanimously by the 71 unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly. The text also toughens penalties for many offences. Archival image of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, at the Second Summit of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) on Security and Development in Bamako, Mali, Tuesday, December 23, 2025 .

Mali.title: MALI: 724 NEW RECRUITS UNDER THE FLAG AT SÉNOU AIR BASE 101, THE 2025 CONTINGENT READY TO PROTECT THE NATION
Mali.summary: The commitment and moral rearmament of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) has reached a new milestone. This Monday, October 19, 2026, the Training Center of the Senou Air Base 101 served as a framework for a solemn takeover marking the end of the Basic Common Training (FCB) for 724 young recruits of the 2025 contingent. A symbolic event of renewal, bravery and dedication to the Fatherland .

Mali.title: Mali: Military Attacks On Civilians, Insurgent Abuses
Mali.summary: Malian armed forces and their allies have since July 2026 responded to mounting attacks by Islamist and separatist armed groups with abusive counterinsurgency operations in central and northern Mali. The Malian military, armed groups, and insurgent forces are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organizations and governments largely stand by.

Mali.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea Near Conflict; Egypt Forms anti-Ethiopia Coalition; Mali Retakes Kidal: Africa File, October 8, 2026
Mali.summary: October 08, 2026 Ethiopia and Eritrea Near Conflict; Egypt Forms anti-Ethiopia Coalition; Mali Retakes Kidal: Africa File, October 8, 2026 Authors: Liam Karr and Michael DeAngelo Contributors: Alexander Brown and Victoria Hutchinson Key Takeaways: - Ethiopia. Ethiopian federal forces captured the Tigray regional capital Mekele and have advanced north and west toward operationally significant towns, likely spurring Eritrea to deploy a limited number of reinforcements into northern Ethiopia to support the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, although reported Eritrean incursions are unconfirmed.

Burkina Faso.title: Image Published on October 21, 2026 Africa Burkina: Reinstating the death penalty risks being used to "crack down on dissent", according to HRW Reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso is a "chilling message" sent to opponents in this junta-ruled country and risks being...
Burkina Faso.summary: Reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso risks being used to "crack down on dissent", according to HRW The reinstatement of the death penalty in Burkina Faso is a "chilling message" to opponents in the junta-ruled country and risks being used as "a new tool to crack down on dissent", human rights NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) warned on Wednesday. . Burkina is led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who came to power after a military coup in September 2022.

Burkina Faso.title: Fight against terrorism, Burkina Faso reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The Government of Burkina Faso had put forward the idea in the Council of Ministers on 4 December. Nearly a year later, the transitional parliament unanimously voted on a new penal code that reinstates the death penalty, although it has been abolished since May 2018. Acts of terrorism, espionage, treason, or even parricide and the import of expired or prohibited products, resulting in death, are punishable by death.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina: the death penalty reintroduced in the Penal Code
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly of Burkina Faso adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the draft law on the Penal Code, thus enacting the reintroduction of the death penalty, which had been abolished in 2018. The draft law revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso was adopted on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, by the People's Legislative Assembly .

Burkina Faso.title: Turkish gendarmes in immersion at the national gendarmerie of Burkina
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish Gendarmerie is staying in Ouagadougou, as part of a working visit and consolidation of the partnership with the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso. This mission is led by Lieutenant General Aykut TANRIVERDI, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of the Republic of Türkiye . It is with the rise of colors, a highly solemn act and rich in symbols that the Turkish delegation began its immersion within the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Parliament Votes To Restore Capital Punishment
Burkina Faso.summary: By Enyichukwu Enemanna Burkina Faso’s parliament on Tuesday adopted a revised penal code that reinstates death penalty, nearly a decade after it was abolished in the West African country, the Justice Ministry said in a statement. The revised penal code reintroduces the death penalty for crimes including terrorism, espionage, treason and importing expired or banned products that result in death, government-owned news organisations said.

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: a delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie in immersion at the national gendarmerie of Burkina Faso
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish Gendarmerie is staying in Ouagadougou, as part of a working visit and consolidation of the partnership with the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso. This mission is led by Lieutenant General Aykut TANRIVERDI, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of the Republic of Türkiye . It is with the rise of colors, a highly solemn act and rich in symbols that the Turkish delegation began its immersion within the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso .

Burkina Faso.title: Murders: "Families of victims of crimes, we ask for the lifting of defence secrecy"
Burkina Faso.summary: Below, a forum of victims and members of the secret defense collective, of which the International Network, Justice for Thomas Sankara and his companions is a member. This op-ed is in particular signed by Mariam Sankara, Aïda Kiemdé and Céline Bamouni, respectively daughter of Frédéric Kiemdé and Paulin Bamouni, murdered alongside Thomas Sankara on 15 October 1987 in Ouagadougou .

Burkina Faso.title: Forum: "Families of victims of crimes, we ask for the lifting of defence secrecy"
Burkina Faso.summary: Below, a Tribune of victims and members of the secret defense collective, of which the International Network, Justice for Thomas Sankara and his companions is a member. This op-ed is in particular signed by Mariam Sankara, Aïda Kiemdé and Céline Bamouni, respectively daughter of Frédéric Kiemdé and Paulin Bamouni, murdered alongside Thomas Sankara on 15 October 1987 in Ouagadougou .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: the new Penal Code provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the People's Legislative Assembly adopted a new Penal Code in Burkina Faso. The text provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty for certain offences, including terrorism, treason, espionage and parricide. The import of expired or prohibited products resulting in death is also concerned.

Burkina Faso.title: Ten suspects arrested in an alleged QNET case
Burkina Faso.summary: The Sangalkam Territorial Brigade arrested ten foreign nationals on Monday, October 19, 2026, in Kounoune Centrale, Senegal, following information indicating the presumed presence of a network linked to QNET. Investigations continue to determine the scope of this network's activities and establish the responsibilities of the defendants The operation carried out by the Sangalkam Territorial Brigade led to the arrest of ten individuals of different nationalities.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Parliament adopts the reinstatement of the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, by 71 votes, the new Penal Code reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso. The new Code was passed on 20 October 2026, eight years after the abolition of the death penalty in the country . The Minister of Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, justifies this reform by the need to modernize the legal framework, strengthen security, fight against terrorism and protect populations.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso - The ruling junta reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: - Burkina Faso: La junte au pouvoir rétablit la peine de mort RFI, 21 Octobre 2026 les 71 députés burkinabè ont adopté à l'unanimité, mardi 20 octobre, un nouveau code pénal qui réintroduit la peine capitale… Plus » les 71 députés burkinabè ont adopté à l'unanimité, mardi 20 octobre, un nouveau code pénal qui réintroduit la peine capitale pour un certain nombre de crimes en lien avec le terrorisme, l'espionnage, la trahison ou encore l'importation de produits périmés ou prohibés susceptibles d'entraîner la mort.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: The new Penal Code reintroduces the death penalty for certain offences
Burkina Faso.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the draft law revising the Burkinabe Criminal Code. Defended by the Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, the text reintroduces the death penalty for certain offences, in particular those related to terrorism, espionage and treason . Meeting in plenary session, the 71 parliamentarians approved the draft law on the review of Law No.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso adopts a new penal code reinstating the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: The death penalty had been abolished in Burkina Faso in 2018 The deputies of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) of Burkina Faso adopted on Tuesday evening, unanimously by 71 voters, the draft law on the Penal Code which reinstates the death penalty for certain offences including acts of terrorism and espionage . According to the new penal code, acts of terrorism, espionage, treason, parricide and the importation of expired or prohibited products resulting in death are now punishable by death, explained the Minister of Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, after the vote .

Burkina Faso.title: "Sentimentalism is over": in Burkina Faso, Ibrahim Traoré reinstates the death penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: Eight years after its abolition, the death penalty was reintroduced this Tuesday in the Burkinabe penal code. A security shift assumed by the junta in power, which sees it as a way to fight terrorism and espionage . Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new penal code on Tuesday, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA).

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: Burkina Faso and Türkiye explore new avenues for collaboration between their gendarmeries
Burkina Faso.summary: A delegation of the Turkish Gendarmerie, led by Lieutenant General Aykut Tanriverdi, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of Türkiye, makes a working visit to Ouagadougou . The announcement is made this Wednesday, October 21 by the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso, specifying that this visit is part of the strengthening of military cooperation between the two countries .

Burkina Faso.title: 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces: a popular cross-country to kick off the festivities
Burkina Faso.summary: The National Armed Forces organized a popular cross, under the sign of cohesion, as part of the commemorative activities of their 66th anniversary, Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou. As part of the commemoration of their 66th anniversary, the National Armed Forces (FAN) kicked off activities on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou On this occasion, a popular cross-country race was organized in the afternoon that mobilized elements of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS), paramilitary bodies and civilian populations.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso reinstates death penalty: Justice ministry
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso has reinstated the death penalty following a unanimous vote by the country’s unelected legislature, the Justice Ministry announced Tuesday. The new penal code reverses the abolition of capital punishment in 2018. Authorities say the move aims to strengthen public order, uphold national values and improve security.

Niger.title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches : What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
Niger.summary: The mutiny that broke out in air base 101 in Niamey in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the ‘jihadists.’ For all of the Sahel, it’s a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.

Niger.title: Military cooperation: Algeria and Niger sign a partnership agreement
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger want to strengthen their exchanges in the field of defence. This Wednesday, October 21, in Algiers, Chief of Staff Saïd Chanegriha and that of Niger, Salifou Modi signed a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation between the two countries. Said Chanegriha, expressed the readiness of the Algerian army to examine any Nigerian proposal aimed at consolidating their military and security relations .

Niger.title: Agadez: Burial of the bodies of a dozen victims of the armed attack on the Arlit-Agadez axis
Niger.summary: Agadez, Oct. 21 (ANP) – The Governor of the Agadez Region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa attended, on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the removal of the bodies, followed by the burial of the victims of the attack against the SONITRAV buses on the Arlit–Agadez axis.

Niger.title: Insecurity: the authorities of Agadez on maximum alert after an armed attack that killed twelve people on the Tchiro-Agadez axis
Niger.summary: The Governor of the Agadez region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, chaired an emergency meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. Several items were on the agenda of the forum, including, among others, the examination and analysis of the security situation in the region, with a particular focus on the attack on the two SONITRAV buses, which occurred on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, on the Tchirozérine-Agadez.

Niger.title: Niger: two Western hostages released in Libya after more than a year and a half at the hands of the Islamic State
Niger.summary: Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique Détenues au Niger par l’État islamique pendant plus d’un an et demi, Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher ont été libérées et sont arrivées à Benghazi. La médiation a été orchestrée par Saddam Haftar, désireux d’asseoir son influence politique au Sahel. C’est la fin d’un long calvaire pour Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher.

Niger.title: Lieutenant General Said Chanegriha receives the Minister of National Defence of the Republic of Niger
Niger.summary: Lieutenant General Said Chanegriha, Minister Delegate to the Minister of National Defence and Chief of Staff of the People's National Army, receives on Wednesday the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Niger, Lieutenant General Salifou Modi.

Niger.title: Algeria Deploys Military to Bolster Sahel Security
Niger.summary: Algeria’s decision in August to deploy elements of its military to support Niger’s ruling junta was more than simply a policy shift: It showed that one of Africa’s strongest militaries is prepared to project its power in the name of maintaining stability in the Sahel, according to analysts. The day after the Aug. 29 mutiny by a group of Nigerien soldiers, Algeria dispatched four Sukhoi Su-30 fighter jets and an air-to-air refueling plane to Niger’s Air Base 101 in Niamey.

On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the use of precise information made it possible to detect and follow several columns of motorcyclists moving in the Ouagadou forest, near the village of Ngoma Koura.

Mali.title: Night rounds to secure IDP sites
Mali.summary: In Gao, Macina, Bankass and Sévaré, IDPs and refugees face security challenges: theft of equipment, vandalism and lack of monitoring capacity. To protect their property and prevent incidents, some communities organize themselves into safety committees and multiply night rounds. But these local initiatives remain fragile and residents are demanding more protection .

Mali.title: 48 people were killed in Mali by an attack by a group affiliated with ISIS
Mali.summary: Forty-eight people were killed in the Menaka region in eastern Mali following an attack by a group affiliated with ISIS, a lawmaker told the Associated Press. Musa Asharatomani, a Tuareg leader and member of the National Transitional Council, said that ISIS fighters in the coastal province attacked the area on Sunday evening and until Monday morning, and the victims included children and the elderly.

Mali.summary: The security situation in the Sikasso Region remains under surveillance, after an attempted attack on the Mamassoni checkpoint on the Zanadougou road.
